newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel shares hit all-time high.
newsitem.headline: Israel shares hit all-time high.

text.p: Israeli shares rose to an all-time high on Wednesday, traders said.
The benchmark Mishtanim index of top 100 shares rose 2.48 percent, or 6.29 points, to 259.95 on a high all-share turnover of 210 million shekels against 252 million shekels on Tuesday.
The previous high was reached on November 11, 1994, when the Mishtanim reached 258.44.
The Maof 25 blue chip index closed 2.97 percent higher at 269.01.

"Nothing can spoil the party. Even the terrible air crash did not prevent the market from rising," said Uri Schur at Eyal Securities referring to a military accident on Tuesday in which two helicopters collided killing 73 Israeli soldiers.
"The market is rising too fast and it is very volatile. The market is becoming very risky and a correction must come. It can not rise for ever," Schur added.
Baruch Glicksberg at Clal Insurance said: "The market is showing strength and everybody is buying -- institutional investors, mutual funds, portfolio managers and foreign investors."
Glicksberg unlike Schur said all the technical indicators showed the market would continue to rise.
The most active share was Israel Chemicals which rose 3.0 percent to 387 agorot on volume of 13.3 million shekels.

Bank Leumi, the second most active share, surged 7.0 percent to 530 agorot on turnover of 12.4 million shekels. In a report released on Wednesday Salomon Brothers said it had assigned Bank Leumi a buy rating.
Salomon said it expected Leumi to continue a recovery in "core" earnings that began in 1995 into 1997 and 1998.
Koor Industries gained 3.75 percent to 35,234 agorot on volume of 11.8 million shekels.
